title: Collection of Mouse Cerebrospinal Fluid from the Cisterna Magna
author: Aisha Sati

steps.title: Expose cisterna magna
steps.instruction: Perform blunt dissection with forceps to separate subcutaneous tissue and the m. biventer cervicis and m. rectus capitis dorsalis major muscles until the dura is visible, taking care not to pinch or damage the dura; retract the overlying muscles to each side to fully expose the cisterna magna.

steps.title: Prepare capillary assembly
steps.instruction: Pull glass capillaries with a micropipette puller, mount a sharpened capillary on a micromanipulator, connect its opposite end to thin tubing attached to a syringe, break the tip at a ~40° angle so the opening is ~10‑20 µm, then push out air from the syringe and fix the assembly on the descending arm of the stereotaxic apparatus.

substeps.instruction: Pull glass capillary using a micropipette puller.
Mount the sharpened capillary on a micromanipulator and attach thin tubing to a syringe.
Break the tip with straight forceps at ~40° angle, leaving a 10‑20 µm opening.
Expel air from the syringe and secure the assembly on the descending arm of the stereotaxic apparatus.

steps.title: Anesthetize and secure mouse
steps.instruction: Inject intraperitoneally 0.15 ml Nimatek + 0.20 ml Domitor + 1.5 ml sterile saline (dose 0.1 ml per 10 g body weight); confirm anesthesia by toe‑pinch response, place the mouse on a heating pad, and fix the head in the stereotaxic frame with ear bars.

steps.title: Incise neck and expose muscles
steps.instruction: Trim fur on the dorsal neck, make a sagittal skin incision followed by small lateral incisions to expose the underlying muscles, and clean the surgical field with saline‑moistened cotton buds to remove blood and hair.

steps.title: Insert capillary into cisterna
steps.instruction: Using the prepared capillary, pierce the dura of the cisterna magna so that the tip lies within the cavity without contacting tissue or vessels; aim for the middle of the triangular area away from major blood vessels.

steps.title: Collect cerebrospinal fluid
steps.instruction: Apply gentle negative pressure by pulling the syringe plunger while observing the capillary under the microscope; when the cisterna refills (indicated by vessel pulsation), repeat the gentle suction to draw additional CSF.

substeps.instruction: Pull syringe plunger to create slight negative pressure and watch CSF entry.
Allow the cisterna to refill; when normal pressure returns (vessel pulsates), apply more negative pressure to collect further CSF.

steps.title: Withdraw capillary
steps.instruction: Wait until the pressure in the cisterna returns to normal, then carefully remove the capillary from the cavity.

steps.title: Transfer CSF to tube
steps.instruction: Collect the CSF from the capillary into a protein low‑binding Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge CSF sample
steps.instruction: Spin the CSF at 10 000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes; transfer the supernatant to a new protein low‑binding Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Store samples at -80°C
steps.instruction: Place the final CSF aliquots at –80 °C for storage.

steps.title: Troubleshoot head angle
steps.instruction: If the triangular landmark is not clearly visible or CSF does not enter the capillary, adjust the head angle of the mouse.
